Corollary 7.12

Let \(E\) be a \(\mathcal{U}\)-category admitting a small generating subcategory \(C\), and such that every object of \(E\) is the source of a monomorphism into an object injective of \(E\). Suppose moreover that for every \(T \in \mathrm{ob}\, C\), the sum \(T \sqcup T\) in \(E\) is representable, and that every morphism with source \(T \sqcup T\) factors as an epimorphism effective followed by a monomorphism. Then \(E\) admits a full cogenerating subcategory \(D\). More precisely, one can take \(D\) such that \(\mathrm{card}\,\mathrm{ob}\, D \leq \prod_{T,T'\in\mathrm{ob}\, C} 2^{\mathrm{card}(\mathrm{Hom}(T',T\sqcup T))^2}\).

Let \(C\) be a \(\mathcal{U}\)-site. proposals.before: Proof. We shall limit ourselves to giving indications. We leave to the reader the task of showing that the covering families in the sense of 5.2 are the covering families of a topology \(T_C\) on \(\widehat{C}\) (one uses 4.1). The covering families of the canonical topology on \(\widehat{C}\) are the epimorphic families on \(\widehat{C}\) (2.6 and I 3.1). Since \(a\) commutes with inductive limits (4.1), the topology \(T_C\) is finer than the canonical topology of \(\widehat{C}\). Moreover the covering families of \(C\) are covering families of \(T_C\) (5.1). If, then, \(T'\) denotes the least fine of the topologies of \(\widehat{C}\) possessing the properties a) and b), \(T_C\) is finer than \(T'\). Let \((f_i : H_i \to K)\), \(i \in I\), be a covering family of \(T_C\). Let us show that \((f_i, i \in I)\) is a family covering of \(T'\). Let \(s_i : H_i \to H = \coprod H_i\) be the canonical monomorphisms and \(f = (f_i, i \in I) : H = \coprod_i H_i \to K\) the morphism defined by the \(f_i\). The family of the \(s_i\) is covering for \(T'\). To show that \((f_i, i \in I)\) is a covering family of \(T'\), it therefore suffices to show, by virtue of axiom (T2) of topologies, that the morphism \(f : H \to K\) is covering for \(T'\). There exists an epimorphic family of \(\widehat{C}\), \(u_\lambda : X_\lambda \to K\), \(\lambda \in \Lambda\), \(X_\lambda \in \mathrm{ob}\, C\) (I 3.4). To show that \(f : H \to K\) is covering for \(T'\), it therefore suffices, by virtue of axiom (T 2) of topologies, to show that for every \(\lambda \in \Lambda\), the morphism \(\mathrm{pr}_2 : H \times_K X_\lambda \to X_\lambda\) is covering for \(T'\). Let then \(v_j : Y_j \to H \times_K X_\lambda\), \(j \in J\), \(Y_j \in \mathrm{ob}\, C\), be an epimorphic family of \(\widehat{C}\). The family \((\mathrm{pr}_2 \circ v_j, j \in J)\) is covering for \(T_C\). It is therefore a covering family of \(C\) (5.1). It is therefore a covering family of \(T'\). Consequently the sieve generated by \(\mathrm{pr}_2 : H \times_K X_\lambda \to X_\lambda\) contains a sieve covering for \(T'\). It is therefore covering for \(T'\) and consequently \(\mathrm{pr}_2 : H \times_K X_\lambda \to X_\lambda\) is covering, q.e.d.

Proposition 1.2

Let \(C\) be a small site, \(C'\) a \(\mathcal{U}\)-site and \(u : C \to C'\) a functor between the underlying categories. The following properties are equivalent:

  1. i)

    The functor \(u\) is continuous.

  2. ii)

    For every object \(X\) of \(C\) and every sieve \(R \hookrightarrow X\) covering \(X\), the morphism \(u_! R \to u(X)\) is bicovering in \(\widehat{C}'\) (II 5.2 and I 5.1).(∗)

  3. iii)

    For every bicovering family \(H_i \to K\), \(i \in I\), of \(\widehat{C}\), the family of the \(u_! H_i \to u_! K\), \(i \in I\), is bicovering in \(\widehat{C}'\).

  4. iv)

    There exists a functor \(u^s : \widetilde{C} \to \widetilde{C}'\), commuting with inductive limits and "extending \(u\)", i.e. such that the diagram of canonical functors \[ \xymatrix{ C \ar[r]^-{u} \ar[d]_-{\varepsilon_C} & C' \ar[d]^-{\varepsilon_{C'}} \\ \widetilde{C} \ar[r]_-{u^s} & \widetilde{C}' } \] is commutative up to isomorphism.

Moreover, when \(C\) is no longer necessarily a small site, but a \(\mathcal{U}\)-site, we always have i) \(\Longleftrightarrow\) iv) and the functor \(u^s\) of iv) is necessarily a left adjoint of the functor \(u_s : \widetilde{C}' \to \widetilde{C}\), and is consequently determined up to unique isomorphism.

Exercise 4.16

We say that a topos \(E\) is generated by its opens if the opens of \(E\) (i.e. the subobjects of the final object \(e\) of \(E\)) form a generating family (I 7). Such a topos possesses the property following:

(P) Every epimorphic family \(X_i \longrightarrow X\), \(i \in I\), is dominated by a family epimorphic \(U_j \longrightarrow X\), \(j \in J\), where the \(U_j \longrightarrow X\) are monomorphisms.

a) Do there exist topoi that possess property (P) and that are not generated by their opens? The topoi associated to topological spaces are generated by their opens. If \(E\) is generated by its opens (resp. enjoys (P)), then for every object \(X\) of \(E\), \(E_{/X}\) is generated by its opens (resp. enjoys (P)). Every subtopos of a topos generated by its opens is generated by its opens. Property (P) is not a property of local character.

b) Let \(E\) be a topos and \(\operatorname{Ouv}(E)\) the category of opens of \(E\) equipped with the topology induced. The inclusion functor \(\operatorname{Ouv}(E) \longrightarrow E\) is a morphism of sites, whence a morphism of topoi \(\Pi : E \longrightarrow \widetilde{\operatorname{Ouv}(E)}\). The functor \(\Pi^*\) is fully faithful. The morphism \(\Pi\) possesses, with respect to the 2-category of topoi generated by their opens, a universal property which the reader will make explicit.

c) Let \(E\) be a topos generated by its opens and \(\operatorname{Point}(E)\) the set of points up to isomorphism of \(E\). Show that \(\operatorname{Point}(E)\) is small. Put a topology on \(\operatorname{Point}(E)\) and define a morphism \(\operatorname{Top}(\operatorname{Point}(E)) \longrightarrow \widetilde{\operatorname{Ouv}(E)}\) making \(\operatorname{Top}(\operatorname{Point}(E))\) a subtopos of \(\widetilde{\operatorname{Ouv}(E)}\). For every topological space \(X\), show that every morphism from \(\operatorname{Top}(X)\) to \(E\) yields a morphism from \(\operatorname{Top}(X)\) to \(\operatorname{Top}(\operatorname{Point}(E))\). proposals.before: La première assertion est bien connue (SGA IX 4.10 et 4.11) lorsque \(f\) est de présentation finie ou que \(f\) est plat; le cas général se réduit à celui où \(f\) est de présentation finie. En effet, on sait déjà que le foncteur \(f^*\) est pleinement fidèle (SGA 1 IX 3.4). Il suffit de prouver que \(f^*\) est essentiellement surjectif, i.e. que tout \(Z'\) étale sur \(X'\) "provient" d'un \(Z\) étale sur \(X\). Utilisant le fait que \(f\) est un homéomorphisme universel, et la pleine fidélité de \(f^*\), on est ramené au cas où \(X\), \(X'\), \(Z'\) sont affines, spectres d'anneaux \(A\), \(A'\), \(B'\). Ecrivant \(A'\) comme limite inductive de ses sous-\(A\)-algèbres de type fini \(A'_i\), \(B'\) provient d'une algèbre étale \(B'_i\) sur un \(A'_i\) (cf. On a alors un \(A\) isomorphisme \(A' \simeq A''/J\), ou \(A'' \simeq A[t_1, \ldots t_n]\) et \(J\) est un idéal de \(A''\). Ecrivant \(J\) comme limite inductive de ses sous-idéaux \(J_i\) de type fini, et posant \(A'_i = A''/J_i\), on aura encore \(A' = \varinjlim_i A'_i\), donc \(B'\) provient d'une algèbre étale \(B'_i\) sur un \(A'_i\) (loco citato).
